newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares dip slightly on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares dip slightly on profit-taking.

text.p: The Lima Stock Exchange dipped slightly Wednesday on profit-taking, after six consecutive sessions of gains led by advances in the mining and service sectors, brokers said.
They predicted more profit-taking for Thursday despite the market's firm medium- and long-term perspectives.
"The most important thing is that the economy is improving and therefore these are just technical corrections," said Manuel Torres, of Finvest brokerage.
The general index fell 0.57 percent to 1,675.98 points and the blue-chip selective index was off 0.33 percent to 2,430.77. Trading volume was a moderate 33.8 million soles ($12.9 million).

Prior to Wednesday's profit-taking, the market had been strongly boosted in recent days by the formal closing of Peru's Brady Plan to restructure foreign commercial debt and the January year-on-year economic growth figure of 4.5 percent.
Benchmark Telefonica del Peru fell Tuesday 1.32 percent to six soles on one million shares, while electricity distributor Edelnor was off 1.22 percent to 2.43 soles on 73,000 shares.

"Investors are calm about the future of the market. Now there is confidence to think in the medium- and long-term. There are industrial stocks with attractive prices and part of the capital should be concentrated there in coming days," said Hernando Pastor, of T&J brokerage.
